decision.explanation: The normal equation is AᵀWᵀWAx=AᵀWᵀWb. Since the only row changed by W is the zero row of A, the coefficient matrix is [[5,-10],[-10,20]] and the right-hand side is [1,-2]ᵀ. Thus a=5, b=20, c=1, so a+b+c=26.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -10 \\ -10 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
after.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}5 & -10 \\ -10 & 20\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=5+20+1=26.
$$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $2a+\frac{b}{c}?$
content.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {2}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & -8 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 8 & -16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}24 & -48 \\ -48 & 96\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 24\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}24 & -48 & -12 \\ -48 & 96 & 24\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}24 & -48 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+\frac{b}{c}=2\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+\frac{2}{1}=1.
$$

content.problem:
Find the solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}72 \\ 0 \\ 41\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {3}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}72 \\ 0 \\ 41\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -4 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}72 \\ 0 \\ 369\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}13 & -10 \\ -10 & 26\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}216 \\ 81\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the matrix on the left-hand side is invertible, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & ={[\begin{aligned}13 & -10 \\ -10 & 26\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}216 \\ 81\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{13\cdot 26-(-10)\cdot (-10)}[\begin{aligned}26 & 10 \\ 10 & 13\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}216 \\ 81\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{238}[\begin{aligned}6\,426 \\ 3\,213\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}27 \\ 13.5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -8 \\ -8 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ c\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
content.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{1}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {4}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 8 & 4 \\ -16 & 16\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}32 & -8 \\ -8 & 24\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=32+24+8=64.
$$
